claims.claim: Hook (A4): what a viewer who swipes at ~2 s takes away from 'Pompeii's "mother and child"?' with the tag "MOTHER?" over a gold bracelet
claims.where: spoken (hook, A4) + on-screen: MOTHER? hook tag
claims.source_checked: Pilli et al. 2024, Curr Biol 34(22):5307-5318, doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007 (PMID 39515325, PMC11627482): abstract and Results full text via Firecrawl research index (firecrawl_research_inspect_paper / read_paper). Direct Europe PMC fetch was blocked by the session proxy.
claims.note: At second two the viewer has only a question ('mother and child?', 'MOTHER?'), which asserts nothing false and signals doubt; the answer ('the adult was a man') lands in the same first sentence. The paper's own abstract names the popular reading 'often interpreted as mother and child', so the label of the story is accurate. Passes A4.

claims.claim: Ancient DNA says the adult was a man.
claims.source_checked: doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007, abstract, Results (House of the Golden Bracelet) and Table 1
claims.note: Abstract: the bracelet-wearer 'is genetically an adult male'. Results: 'All individuals were sexed as genetically male, including the presumed female adult (Individual 52)'; Table 1: Ind. 52 genetic sex M, Y haplogroup T1a1a1b2b2b1a. Ind. 52 estimated 'younger middle-aged adult'. 'Man' = adult male; the paper itself uses 'he'. 'The adult' refers to the mother figure; a second adult (Ind. 50) was also found, but the line does not claim otherwise.

claims.source_checked: doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007, Results, House of the Golden Bracelet
claims.note: 'In 1974, four victims were discovered in close vicinity to each other at the site'; Ind. 52 is among 'the first three victims'.

claims.claim: wearing a gold bracelet, beside a small child
claims.source_checked: doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007, Results, House of the Golden Bracelet; abstract
claims.note: 'an intricate golden bracelet of exceptional weight (6.1 grams) worn on one arm'. Child Ind. 51, '5 to 6-year-old', 'apparently standing on Individual 52's hip' (Results) / 'a child on their lap' (abstract). 'Beside' is vaguer than either description but contradicts neither; 'small child' fits a 5-6-year-old ('young child' in the paper).

claims.claim: he was long described as a mother
claims.source_checked: doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007, Results ('Combined genetic and osteological findings...' and House of the Golden Bracelet)
claims.note: 'Individual 52 was traditionally interpreted as a woman and mother, due to the association with the child, and an intricate golden bracelet'; such interpretations were 'spread through museal exhibitions and educational and publicity materials'. The reading dates from 1974, so 'long' (about 50 years) holds. The sentence's implied reasons (bracelet, child) match the paper's stated reasons.

claims.claim: And the DNA found no sign he was related to the child.
claims.source_checked: doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007, Results (House of the Golden Bracelet; DNA preservation section), Discussion, Table 1
claims.note: 'both the mitochondrial DNA and whole genome data found no evidence of biological relatedness, at least up to the third degree, between any of the individuals'. Inds. 51 and 52 both have nuclear data (Table 1: 62,030 and 364,533 SNPs) and different mtDNA (T2c1c vs U1a1), so the test covers this pair. 'No sign' = 'no evidence' and does not exceed the paper (whose Discussion says even more strongly 'in fact not genetically related').

claims.claim: Two victims found close together, read as an embrace, were imagined as sisters, or a mother and daughter.
claims.source_checked: doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007, Results, House of the Cryptoporticus; abstract
claims.note: 'two (Individuals 21 and 22) were found close to each other in what was interpreted as an embrace ... the archaeologists hypothesized that they could be two sisters, mother and daughter, or lovers'. Wording matches; 'lovers' omitted, and the script never claims the DNA excludes that reading.

claims.claim: One of them was genetically male.
claims.source_checked: doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007, Results, House of the Cryptoporticus; Table 1; STAR Methods (quantification)
claims.note: 'The nuclear genetic analysis was successful only for Individual 22 and revealed he was male, excluding the possibility that the pair of victims were sisters or mother and daughter.' Table 1: Ind. 22 genetic sex M. Sample 21 gave no quantification result, so 'one of them' is exact (abstract: 'included at least one genetic male').

claims.claim: The casts were made from 1863 on, by pouring plaster into the hollows the bodies left in the ash.
claims.source_checked: doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007, STAR Methods 'Plaster casts' and Introduction
claims.note: Methods: 'In 1863 Fiorelli set up a method to realize plaster casts ... pouring liquid chalk into the voids left by the bodies in the hardened ash'. Intro: 'pouring liquid plaster into the voids left by decay of the victims' soft tissue. Since then ... 104 plaster casts ... have been produced using Fiorelli's method.' 'From 1863 on' covers the 1914 and 1974 casts.

claims.claim: Over the years, restorers reworked some casts, possibly to make them tell a story.
claims.source_checked: doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007, Introduction and Discussion
claims.note: Intro (stated as fact): 'The casts had been considerably manipulated and likely creatively restored in the past, with stylistic variations between casts in part reflecting aesthetic preferences of the periods in which they were made' and 'restorers who chose to enhance or alter some features of the bodies' shapes' (this rests on the paper's ref. 6, the 2015 imaging, read here only as Pilli reports it). Discussion: 'it is possible that the exploitation of the casts as vehicles for storytelling led to the manipulation of their poses and relative positioning by restorers in the past.' 'Reworked some casts' = manipulated/altered (fact); 'possibly ... tell a story' keeps the paper's 'possible'. The paper does not say these two casts were reworked; the line's 'some casts' / 'a story' does not claim so.

claims.claim: The DNA does not tell us who these people were. It tells us the old stories were guesses.
claims.source_checked: doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007, Introduction, Results, Discussion
claims.note: Interpretations were made 'in the absence of genetic data ... based on the shape and position of the bodies'; scholars and public were 'speculating about the identities of the victims'; the study 'illustrates how unreliable narratives based on limited evidence can be' and warns against 'establishing new narratives'. 'Guesses' is a fair plain rendering of 'speculating'/'unreliable narratives based on limited evidence'. DNA gives sex, kinship and ancestry, not identity, so the first sentence holds.

claims.claim: Had you heard the mother-and-child story?
claims.note: A question to the viewer, not a factual claim. It names the old reading, which the abstract itself calls 'often interpreted as mother and child'.

claims.source_checked: doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007, abstract and Results
claims.note: A question mark over the bracelet asserts nothing false; it is the reading the paper overturns ('traditionally interpreted as a woman and mother ... and an intricate golden bracelet'). The bracelet drawing is a stylised stand-in; the paper describes it only as 'intricate' and 6.1 g, so it should not be presented as the real object's design (keep the ILLUSTRATION label where it is drawn, incl. the thumbnail if space allows).

claims.note: Casts were 'likely creatively restored in the past' and 86 were under restoration from 2015; the 14 sampled casts (incl. 21, 22, 50-53) were 'of the 86 casts undergoing restoration'.
